1. instrument. # Investment Memorandum

## 1. Executive Summary

- On November 18, 2022, eight new subsidiaries of Aramark joined as guarantors to an existing credit agreement originally dated March 28, 2017.
- The borrowers under the original credit facility include multiple Aramark entities across jurisdictions: Aramark Services Inc. (U.S.), Aramark Canada Ltd. (Canada), Aramark Investments Limited and Aramark Limited (U.K.), Aramark Ireland Holdings Limited and Aramark Regional Treasury Europe DAC (Ireland), Aramark Holding Deutschland GmbH (Germany), and Aramark International Finance S.à r.l. (Luxembourg).
- JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A. serves as administrative agent and collateral agent, with multiple lenders participating in the syndicate.
- The new subsidiaries joining as guarantors include Union Supply Group Inc., Union Supply Commissary Solutions Inc., and six Next Level hospitality-related entities (Next Level Hospitality Services LLC, Next Level PEO LLC, NLAL Hospitality LLC, NLNC Hospitality LLC, NLPA Hospitality LLC, and NLSD Hospitality LLC).
- This joinder agreement expands the guarantee coverage by adding these subsidiaries as loan parties and loan guarantors under the existing credit facility, strengthening the lenders' security package.

## 2. Investment Highlights & Risks

### Key Strengths / Credit Positives:
• Enhanced guarantee coverage through addition of eight subsidiary guarantors, potentially improving recovery prospects for lenders
• JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A. as administrative agent represents a tier-1 banking relationship
• Multinational borrower structure across seven jurisdictions suggests diversified revenue base and operational footprint
• Established credit relationship dating to 2017 indicates ongoing lender confidence and relationship stability

### Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:
• Limited financial information available in this joinder document restricts comprehensive credit assessment
• Complex multinational structure across multiple jurisdictions may present operational and legal complexities
• Addition of hospitality-focused subsidiaries may introduce sector-specific risks, though this expands Aramark's service offerings
